caseStudies.title: Are You In?
caseStudies.quote: "...to be in a car and make music? I’ve never done that before. It’s going to be a lot of fun."
caseStudies.introTextHtml:
How do you capture the charm of Modern Korean Culture?

Hyundai came to us with a problem… With the European launch of their new Inster model just around the corner, they needed a musical concept that spoke to the Korean roots of the company but was also relatable to a European audience. We suggested an exciting strategy that avoided cliché and paired South Korea’s own sogumm with Swedish producer DJ Seinfeld to create something new, something quirky, something authentic…
caseStudies.textAfterGalleryHtml:
Engaging Communities Online

We flew both artists to a place no-one called home where they made a brand new track right there inside the car! Of course we documented the whole thing in a four-part content series which built anticipation amongst the fans.

audioPlayer1.title:
Are You In? –
DJ Seinfeld x sogumm

caseStudies.textAfterAudioPlayerHtml:
Bringing it to the Real World

The track was aired globally across a wide range of media but we also ensured this unique collaboration had an official single release via one of the most influential record labels, Ninja Tune. With over 400,000 streams in the first week and glowing coverage in the music press, the only question that remains is… Are You In?

caseStudies.title: No Regrets
caseStudies.introTextHtml:
A Refreshing Start 

There’s nothing more exciting than shaping a brand’s voice from scratch. Devil’s Advocate — a bold new water brand with a taste for trouble — gave us exactly that opportunity. With no sonic history and no rules, we built a musical identity – in cooperation with our friends at design and communications agency GUDBERG NERGER – from the ground up: playful, provocative, and charmingly unconventional.
caseStudies.textAfterGalleryHtml:
Testing The Waters 

We believe every sonic identity starts with a deep understanding of culture, audience and context — because sound without strategy is just noise. Using Sonic Sweetspot, we mapped the landscape and identified electronic music and its subgenres as Devil’s Advocate’s niche. We filtered emerging trends, selected creative partners from this space, and built a living sonic system designed to evolve with the brand.
caseStudies.textAfterAudioPlayerHtml:
A World of Voices

At the heart of Devil’s Advocate lived a mischievous crew of little monsters — each with its own attitude and energy. We translated this into a flexible sonic system: every character received a distinctive voice and musical identity. Cartoonish, bold, and full of personality — yet unified through one unmistakable tonality. Instead of one static sound logo, we created a dynamic cast — giving the brand room to expand its storytelling while always remaining instantly recognizable. 

Bringing Mischief to Life 

At blut, we believe a sonic strategy only works when it lands where culture actually happens. That’s why we brought Devil’s Advocate straight to its audience: festivals, clubs, live music events — places where playful brands naturally belong. These activations generated vibrant social content, turning real-world moments into shareable digital assets. The result: a disruptive launch with no regrets — and no chance of going unnoticed.

caseStudies.title: Re:arranging Perceptions
caseStudies.quote: "This is magical!! Why can't more orchestras and electropop artists collaborate?"
caseStudies.introTextHtml:
How can public broadcasters compete in the age of streaming? 

The Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR) were struggling to attract a Gen Z audience. It’s a common concern for public broadcasters due to the rising popularity of online streaming services. WDR’s digital channels, in particular, lacked the engaging content to interest a younger target group.
caseStudies.textAfterGalleryHtml:
Developing unique cultural platforms 

As music was a primary interest of their target demographic, we developed a concert series which paired some of the hottest upcoming musical talent with the renowned WDR Funkhaus Orchestra. Re:arranged was born and the live events sold out within minutes.
caseStudies.textAfterAudioPlayerHtml:
Engaging Gen Z 

We took the idea even further and turned the whole thing into a YouTube series, which was both critically acclaimed and sits in the top 2% of WDR’s most watched online content, thereby repositioning WDR as a musical tastemaker for the next generation.

caseStudies.internalName: Volkswagen – Bringing It All Back Home
caseStudies.title: Bringing It All Back Home
caseStudies.quote: "When this happened, it legit changed my life"
caseStudies.introTextHtml:
Homecoming

Volkswagen wanted to speak to a new generation of car customers — and they wanted to do it through music. In a unique collaboration with Beats by Dre, the ask was clear: build something bold, emotional, and culturally resonant that feels authentic to both brands’ respective heritages. Together with Grabarz & Partner we set out to create something that didn’t look like a car ad — and didn’t sound like one either. So we leaned into the genre at the core of Beats’ cultural legacy: Hip-Hop. And shot the whole thing at a VW factory, turning an industrial space into a stage for storytelling.
caseStudies.textAfterGalleryHtml:
Building ideas around the music

The big idea: flip the usual script. Let the car build itself around the music. We invited New Orleans rapper Alfred Banks to perform "Homecoming" — a celebratory cut about coming home — right there on the assembly line. With custom sound design created on-site, the rhythms of the factory became part of the final beat.
caseStudies.textAfterAudioPlayerHtml:
Giving the people what they want

We dropped the full-length “factory version” of Homecoming — and it hit. The campaign won multiple international awards for its music concept, sparked fan love across the Hip-Hop community, and resonated deeply with VW’s next-gen target group. And for Alfred Banks, it became a career-defining moment — proof that when artist and brand truly align, everyone wins.

‍

Alfred Banks: Heritage & Home 

“My experience with the VW x Beats By Dre Ad was life changing. It put me on the map & I got to create with some of the hardest working people I’ve ever met over at blut. It made me very proud to represent my hometown of New Orleans. With New Orleans in mind, I made a playlist of 11 songs that all make me feel the heritage and energy of my hometown. Every artist on this playlist is from New Orleans & it’s a wide range of music showing what we do isn’t just what you think of when my city is brought up in musical conversations.”

caseStudies.title: Invention Is Instrumental
caseStudies.quote: "Corporate sound couldn’t be closer to the company."
caseStudies.introTextHtml:
Honestly… how can sound reflect a brand’s products?

With the challenge of creating a new sonic identity for Schüco which was firmly rooted in their primary products, we set about capturing their essence not in the abstract, but tangibly, in the real world.
caseStudies.textAfterGalleryHtml:
Making the product resonate

The solution was simple, we had to invent something totally new - a unique instrument from one of Schüco's top sellers (the aluminium composite frame) - and compose the brand melody on it. Enter the Schücophone …
caseStudies.textAfterAudioPlayerHtml:
A New Design Standard

The activation was one of the most awarded Sonic Branding projects of the year, brought to life across all relevant touchpoints, with the German Design Award stating "The idea [... ] is already ingenious - but the realisation was fantastic.”
